correctness.rationale: The zero-position identity z_i′=max(i,z_i-k) follows by moving precisely min(k,z_i-i) earlier ones past the ith zero. It preserves prefix-zero dominance, so iterated tortoise images are phase-monotone on irrational rotation-coded factors. Adjacent rotation boundaries j=1,...,n-1 have neighboring factors p01s and p10s, which merge iff the shared prefix p contains fewer than k ones; this is equivalent to j alpha<k. The final-bit boundary j=n is excluded by conserved Hamming weight. Counting all and only these boundaries proves rho_{alpha,k}(n)=n+1-min(n-1,floor(k/alpha)), with no infinite inference from computation. A standalone independent implementation checked 114832 finite rational-cycle parameter cases and a Fibonacci-slope approximation. Assumptions alpha irrational, k>=2, n>=1 and exactly binary are explicit.

value.rationale: The explicit recent motivating work asks for tortoise image complexity beyond its Thue--Morse and paperfolding families, including Sturmian shifts. The exact formula covers every irrational slope, length, and iteration, and identifies a nontrivial finite cutoff B_k+1 of Abelian agreement, the subsequent linear-growth regime, and recovery of the underlying slope alpha by the asymptotic cutoffs. The phase-boundary and zero-position lemmas explain the collapse structurally. This is not an arbitrary finite parameter census, and does not claim a larger theorem for all aperiodic words.
